evals.prompt: Review this proposed repository setup: CLAUDE.md copies the root AGENTS.md, while the same worktree and testing rules are copied into every project. Propose a durable layout for the guidance and explain what should be the source of truth.
assertions: The response recommends one source of truth instead of copied AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md content.
The response separates user-level rules from repository-specific rules.
The response recommends a relative CLAUDE.md symlink when appropriate.

evals.prompt: A coding agent repeatedly publishes pull-request bodies with literal escaped newlines. I think the prevention rule belongs in this repository's AGENTS.md. Assess that placement and propose the next action.
assertions: The response does not blindly duplicate the requested rule in the repository AGENTS.md.
The response bases its target decision on scope and source-of-truth evidence rather than the filename in the request.
When the response finds an existing user-level owner, it treats that as a reason not to add a repository rule.

evals.prompt: Simplify a long AGENTS.md by moving its detailed rules into skills. Describe the migration procedure and the validation needed before deleting the original sections.
assertions: The response inventories each atomic source rule and maps every rule to a destination or explicitly approved removal.
The response reverse-audits the destinations for duplicate rules and assigns each rule one authoritative owner unless a thin adapter is intentional.
The response preserves disambiguating examples instead of assuming prose or model capability is enough.
The response requires a static migration contract in addition to behavioral model evals.
The response does not permit unmapped or unapproved deletions.

evals.prompt: Audit this guidance layout after a migration. The user-level AGENTS.md says to confirm the exact target before destructive operations. A repository AGENTS.md says to verify deletion targets before removing files and also documents the repository test command. A cleanup skill says to double-check paths before destructive cleanup. Choose the authoritative owner for each rule and state what to keep or remove.
assertions: The response recognizes the three destructive-operation rules as semantic duplicates even though their wording differs.
The response keeps the shared destructive-operation rule in the user-level AGENTS.md as its single authoritative owner.
The response removes the redundant destructive-operation copies from the repository AGENTS.md and cleanup skill.
The response preserves the repository-specific test command in the repository AGENTS.md.

evals.prompt: Review a user-level guidance setup where ~/.agents/AGENTS.md is the full shared source, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md only instructs Codex to read that source, and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md only imports it. Decide whether the two tool entrypoints are forbidden duplicates and propose the durable layout.
assertions: The response keeps ~/.agents/AGENTS.md as the single content source of truth.
The response treats the Codex instruction and Claude import as intentional thin adapters rather than duplicated guidance content.
The response does not copy the full shared rules into either tool entrypoint.
The response keeps tool-specific metadata or entrypoint syntax in the thin adapters when needed.

evals.prompt: Explain why binary search has logarithmic time complexity in one short paragraph.
assertions: The response accurately explains logarithmic time complexity.
The response stays focused on binary search rather than agent documentation.
